article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Juanita la Lagrimosa × Kalijah
Breeder: Reggae Seeds
THC Content: Variable by phenotype
CBD Content: High
Terpene Profile: myrcene , caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Forest earth, incense, berries, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October 1–15
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Dancehall occupies an important place in the history of CBD-rich cannabis because it predates the modern wave of carefully marketed cannabinoid-ratio marijuana strains . Released by Spain’s Reggae Seeds in 2006, the cultivar combines the breeder’s celebrated Juanita la Lagrimosa mother with a Kalijah male. What emerged was a predominantly sativa marijuana variety offering relatively fast flowering, colorful late-season flowers, complex incense-and-berry aromas, and a clear cerebral effect built for activity rather than sedation. More importantly, individual plants revealed substantial CBD potential, helping make Dancehall an influential breeding parent for later balanced-cannabinoid cultivars. Reggae Seeds still identifies the original genetics as Juanita la Lagrimosa × Kalijah and lists a 60–70-day indoor flowering period with medium-to-high production.
Genetics and Lineage

The pedigree begins with Juanita la Lagrimosa, one of Reggae Seeds breeder Jimi’s signature creations. The breeder identifies Juanita as Reina Madre × Mexican/Afghan genetics, a predominantly sativa cultivar notable not only for its lemon-Haze and fruity-hash character but also for producing individuals with roughly balanced THC and CBD . Kalijah was selected as the male side of Dancehall, and Reggae Seeds has specifically described Kalijah as a CBD carrier used throughout much of its regular seed collection. Crossing these two lines produced a plant that maintained sativa-style psychoactivity while opening the door to cannabinoid profiles very different from THC-dominant weed.

That CBD inheritance is not perfectly uniform, which is why assigning one THC or CBD percentage to every Dancehall plant would be inaccurate. Historical breeder material explains that CBD appeared in some genotypes of the early Reggae Seeds varieties rather than automatically in every seed. Particular selections became famous because of their chemistry. Dancehall #24, for example, was laboratory identified by Reggae Seeds as having an approximately 1:1 THC-to-CBD ratio and later became the mother of Revolution. Dancehall #20 also went on to become an important parent in other CBD-oriented breeding programs.
Effects and Experience

Dancehall was named appropriately. The psychoactive profile is built around movement, sociability, and mental stimulation rather than sinking into a chair. Reggae Seeds describes the effect as fast-acting, cerebral, creative, and long-lasting, with a particular affinity for conversation and social situations. The opening can feel bright and immediate: attention shifts outward, ideas become easier to follow, and music or creative activities can take on greater depth without the heavy physical pressure produced by many indica-dominant hybrids.

CBD-rich phenotypes can feel distinctly different from high-THC marijuana. Instead of escalating rapidly into an overpowering head high, balanced plants may maintain greater mental composure while still producing an obvious change in mood and perception. This variability is central to understanding Dancehall. One seed may lean toward a more traditional sativa experience, while a selected 1:1 phenotype can deliver a clearer and less intoxicating session. Anyone purchasing flower under the Dancehall name should therefore look at the actual cannabinoid analysis rather than assuming every batch carries the same THC-to-CBD relationship.
Medical Benefits

Dancehall became especially significant to medical cannabis breeding because of its capacity to produce meaningful CBD alongside THC. Balanced cannabinoid flower appeals to some patients because it can provide noticeable cannabis effects without the same degree of intoxication associated with very high-THC weed. Depending on the phenotype, consumers may find the cultivar useful when they want to remain communicative, creative, or functional instead of becoming heavily sedated.

That does not make Dancehall a clinically proven treatment for any specific condition. Research into THC and CBD continues to examine their potential roles in pain, anxiety, neurological disorders, sleep, and other areas, but clinical findings involving isolated cannabinoids or standardized preparations cannot automatically be transferred to one named marijuana strain. The most medically relevant feature here is therefore chemical flexibility: verified CBD-rich Dancehall selections can offer a very different cannabinoid ratio from the overwhelmingly THC-dominant cannabis common in today’s market.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Dancehall’s fragrance develops around contrasts rather than one dominant note. Reggae Seeds describes an aromatic range stretching from forest earth and incense to berries, giving the flowers an almost woodland character underneath their sweeter side. Break apart a mature bud and damp earth, dry herbs, resin, and incense can appear first before softer red-fruit and berry scents begin to emerge.

The flavor lingers noticeably after inhalation. Earth and spice create the foundation, followed by fruitier tones that can suggest berries or sweet herbs. Certain phenotypes may emphasize incense and hash-like depth, while others move toward brighter fruit. Modern databases sometimes assign specific dominant terpenes to Dancehall, but the original breeder does not publish a standardized terpene analysis. For an old regular-seed population with documented cannabinoid variation, treating terpene expression as phenotype-dependent is considerably more accurate than giving the cultivar one immutable chemical profile.
Growing Information

Despite its sativa dominance, Dancehall does not demand the extreme flowering times associated with many tropical marijuana varieties. Reggae Seeds specifies approximately 60–70 days indoors and an outdoor finish between October 1 and October 15 in the Northern Hemisphere. Plants are described as relatively uniform and medium-to-high yielding, with limited lateral branching compared with many sativas. That architecture makes the strain particularly appropriate for Sea of Green cultivation. The breeder recommends moving young plants into flowering at roughly three weeks of age when using that approach.

Outdoors, the plant develops into a compact and robust specimen well adapted to Mediterranean conditions. One of its most visually appealing characteristics can appear late in bloom: when temperatures fall below approximately 20°C, flowers and surrounding plant tissue may develop pronounced purple coloration. Indoor growers should maintain good airflow around ripening flowers and avoid excessive humidity as buds gain density. Since the original regular line can display meaningful cannabinoid variation, growers interested specifically in CBD production may also need laboratory testing and phenotype selection rather than relying on appearance alone.
FAQ
Is Dancehall an indica or sativa?
Dancehall is predominantly sativa. Reggae Seeds does not publish a precise percentage split for the original regular line, but both its growth and cerebral effects lean toward the sativa side.
What are the genetics of Dancehall?

The official genetics are Juanita la Lagrimosa × Kalijah. Juanita itself comes from Reina Madre crossed with Mexican/Afghan genetics, while Kalijah contributed important CBD-carrying traits to the Reggae Seeds breeding program.
Is Dancehall a high-CBD strain?

Some phenotypes are. The original regular seed population does not have one guaranteed CBD percentage, but selected plants have demonstrated substantial CBD. Dancehall #24 was specifically tested by Reggae Seeds at an approximately 1:1 THC-to-CBD ratio.
What does Dancehall taste like?
The breeder describes aromas ranging from forest soil and incense to berries. The smoke can combine earthy, herbal, spicy, resinous, and sweet fruit notes that remain on the palate after exhalation.
How long does Dancehall take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days. Outdoors in the Northern Hemisphere, Reggae Seeds places maturity between October 1 and October 15.
Final Thoughts on Dancehall

Dancehall matters for reasons that reach beyond flavor or yield. Created during the early years of Reggae Seeds, the cultivar helped demonstrate that cannabis could combine a genuinely enjoyable sativa experience with substantial CBD expression. Juanita la Lagrimosa supplies much of that cannabinoid heritage, while Kalijah reinforces the CBD potential and contributes to a plant that remains practical enough for ordinary indoor and outdoor cultivation .

Its personality is equally distinctive. Forest earth, incense, berries, occasional purple coloration, and a quick cerebral high give the weed an unmistakably old-school European breeding character. Add a manageable 60–70-day flowering period and the possibility of balanced THC/CBD phenotypes, and Dancehall becomes more than an interesting Spanish sativa. It is one of the strains that helped lay the groundwork for the modern CBD-rich cannabis category while remaining an appealing cultivar in its own right.
